current_yield: The annual income (interest or dividends) divided by the current price of the security. Measures the return on investment at the current market price.
pe_ratio: Price-to-Earnings ratio. A valuation ratio comparing a company's current share price to its earnings per share. Higher P/E suggests investors expect higher growth.
compound_interest: Interest calculated on the initial principal and also on the accumulated interest of previous periods.
coupon_rate: The annual interest rate paid on a bond, expressed as a percentage of the face value.
face_value: The nominal or dollar value of a security as stated by the issuer. For bonds, it's the amount paid at maturity.
earnings_per_share: The portion of a company's profit allocated to each outstanding share of common stock.
market_price: The current price at which an asset or service can be bought or sold.
dividend_yield: A financial ratio showing how much a company pays in dividends each year relative to its stock price.
